amendment_log.summary: Retained every v1 case and added governed production satisfiability and exploit-path controls under issue 828.

analysis_rules.case_coverage: Every claim class has a positive and negative case, including unsupported classes.
analysis_rules.failure_policy: A required supported positive failure, accepted single-defect negative, failed evidence replay, or missing join refutes that bounded claim class.
analysis_rules.immutability_policy: A product correction creates a new execution snapshot; it never overwrites a failed observation.
analysis_rules.participant_coverage: Every participant obligation has distinct positive and negative executable fixture references.
analysis_rules.unsupported_policy: A class remains untested only when no governed production entrypoint runs; historical unsupported controls do not erase distinct supported controls added by a later protocol revision.

claim_classes.boundary: Closed SDL source shape, field, type, vocabulary, and local constraint validation only.
claim_classes.label: Schema validity
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: The negative case is accepted, the positive control is rejected, or the result is inferred from a generated schema rather than the published production path.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: The positive control is accepted and the single-defect unknown-field case is rejected by the production source/model boundary.

claim_classes.boundary: Static fail-closed cross-reference, ambiguity, cycle, participant-boundary, and related domain invariants over parsed or instantiated SDL.
claim_classes.label: Semantic consistency
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: A named negative passes, a positive control fails, or a test-local oracle is promoted to universal semantic correctness.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: The named positive controls pass and the single-defect dangling-reference and participant-semantics negatives are rejected through production semantic or contract entrypoints.

claim_classes.boundary: Reachability in one named graph with declared node and edge semantics; this protocol exercises workflow control flow only.
claim_classes.label: Graph reachability
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: The unreachable step passes or the workflow witness is promoted to network, participant, service, or exploit reachability.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: A reachable workflow passes and a single unreachable step is rejected by the production semantic validator.

claim_classes.boundary: Existence or non-existence of a model for an explicitly named whole-scenario constraint system and domain.
claim_classes.label: Constraint satisfiability
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: Local predicates, finite envelope membership, witness generation, or topological acyclicity are presented as whole-scenario satisfiability.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: A governed solver proves the satisfiable control and rejects the unsatisfiable control under a pinned theory and domain.

claim_classes.boundary: A typed attack transition graph with prerequisites, effects, observations, and an executable path query or proof.
claim_classes.label: Exploit-path validity
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: Vulnerability references, network links, ACLs, objectives, or successful deployment are presented as exploit-path proof.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: A governed analyzer accepts the valid path and rejects the invalid path over a pinned attack-graph contract.

claim_classes.boundary: Repeatability under named inputs, stage, environment variation, serializer, and equivalence relation; this protocol covers parse-to-compile output only.
claim_classes.label: Determinism and stability
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: The same input drifts, the comparison is vacuous, or parse-to-compile stability is promoted to runtime, replay, backend, or study stability.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: The same fixture compiles to the same canonical digest twice and a distinct fixture produces a distinct digest.

claim_classes.boundary: A governed intervention or ablation comparison under a named causal model and necessity criterion.
claim_classes.label: Counterfactual necessity
claim_classes.objective_fail_criteria: Attribution vocabulary, temporal order, replay labels, or ordinary negative fixtures are presented as counterfactual proof.
claim_classes.objective_pass_criteria: A pinned protocol distinguishes a necessity witness from a non-necessity control across governed worlds.

participant_obligations.label: Participant-local outcomes separated from objective, evaluation, and reward layers

research_question: Which bounded RAES validation claims reproduce at the pinned revision, including the governed finite-domain satisfiability and typed exploit-path production entrypoints?
title: RAES formal semantic-validation, satisfiability, and exploit-path retest
